extracted.intended_audience: scholars, students, and bibliographers studying Francis Bacon and the Novum Organum
extracted.subtask_description: Annotated bibliography and critical introduction to Francis Bacon's Novum Organum, surveying translations, editions, criticisms, and the historiography of Bacon's influence and methods. Intended to guide scholarly judgment about texts, translations, and secondary literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical status: philosopher vs. dilettante
rubrics_metrics.description: "Was Bacon really a Philosopher,' and he answers that, in the proper sense of the word, he was not; he was a genius, but, at the same time, a Dilettante (ein geistreicher Dilettant)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether Bacon's work qualifies as philosophical in the rigorous sense (systematic theory-building) versus being genial but dilettantish; note the distinction that "Aus allgemeinen Gesichtspunkten raisonniren ist noch nicht philosophiren" (reasoning from general points of view is not necessarily philosophizing). Use this criterion to judge depth, systematicity, and seriousness of Bacon's philosophical method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to experimental enquiry and emphasis on facts
rubrics_metrics.description: "That Bacon, however, did great service in spreading a taste for experimental enquiry and in drawing the popular attention to the importance of consulting facts, is allowed throughout the enquiry."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess positive historical contribution by measuring how a work (or author) promoted experimental investigation and attention to empirical facts. Even if other faults exist, weigh this service as a substantive merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigour and character of empirical observations (Sylva Sylvarum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Liebig and Lasson lay considerable stress on the crude character of many of the observations and experiments recorded in the Sylva Sylvarum; neglect of quantitative relations, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge empirical material for concreteness, completeness, and quantitative rigor. Antipatterns include 'an indigested heap of particulars' and neglecting measurements/quantitative relations; defenses note that even so the Sylva may be 'the best and most complete single collection of the kind' up to its time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and accuracy of secondary criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: "This work, which is extremely bitter in tone, and often very inaccurate, contributes nothing new to the knowledge or appreciation of Bacon's philosophy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating scholarly critiques, consider tone (invective vs. balanced) and factual accuracy. Bitter, hyperbolic, or inaccurate treatments are flagged as contributing little; examples given include Liebig's diatribe and translators/blunders that misrepresent sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge: atheism
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the principal accusations summarized against Bacon: '1st, he was an atheist.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a substantive historical/interpretive charge to be assessed by examining Bacon's texts and context. The introduction notes it as a recurring accusation and examines it elsewhere; use primary-text evidence and contextual scholarship to evaluate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge: plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the principal accusations summarized against Bacon: '2nd, he was a plagiarist.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate claims of unacknowledged borrowing by tracing sources, dates, and the originality of formulations. The bibliography frames this as a notable historical criticism to be addressed in detailed scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge: superficiality (smatterer)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the principal accusations summarized against Bacon: '3rd, he was a smatterer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether Bacon's treatments are superficial or show a lack of mastery; look for depth, systematic argumentation, and command of subject matter versus scattered or half-formed assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge: lack of influence on later science
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the principal accusations summarized against Bacon: '4th, his works have had no influence in the subsequent progress of science.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure intellectual influence by tracing citations, adoption of methods, and explicit acknowledgements in later scientific works; consider both popularizing effects and technical impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge: methods defective or inapplicable
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the principal accusations summarized against Bacon: '5th, his proposed methods of investigation are defective, if not false, in statement, and inapplicable in practice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate Bacon's methodological prescriptions for internal coherence and practical applicability. Test claims about induction/experimental methods against historical outcomes and modern standards of method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation accuracy and adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticisms of translations and translators appear repeatedly (e.g., 'M. de Tchihatchef has a wonderful faculty of blundering'; translator 'very careless or having a very imperfect knowledge of the German language').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge translations for fidelity to the original text, completeness (epitome vs full translation), linguistic competence of translator, and presence/absence of errors that mislead readers. Beware of careless translators and partial epitomes that omit important material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edition/editorial quality (notes, indices, prefaces, annotations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain editions (e.g., Kitchin's annotated edition; the Clarendon Press, the Ellis, Spedding, and Heath edition) are praised for indices, notes, prefaces and making the work procurable. 'No student of Bacon's philosophy can now dispense with the five volumes...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate editions by their critical apparatus: accuracy and usefulness of notes, indices, introductions, textual apparatus, and accessibility. Editions with comprehensive annotations and reliable apparatus are considered indispensable for scholars and students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness vs epitome/abridgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to an English epitome published in 1676 'translated and taken out of the Latin by M.D. B D' and other partial translations or private printings (e.g., a translation of the First Book only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a translation/edition is full or abridged and how omissions affect interpretation. Epitomes can mislead if treated as substitutes for the complete work; mark partial translations clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographical accuracy and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations that some bibliographical accounts are inaccurate (e.g., 'Bouillet's bibliographical account, generally, is not very accurate'; references to mistaken edition reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify edition information against primary catalogues and library holdings; do not rely uncritically on secondary bibliographical statements. Accuracy in dates, printers, and edition formats is essential for sound bibliographical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of critical commentaries and prior scholarship to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise for works whose remarks and illustrations are 'of peculiar value to an Editor of the Novum Organum' (e.g., Playfair, Kitchin, Whewell), and notes on which studies are 'of great importance' to the study of Bacon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing or evaluating editions and studies, consider whether prior commentaries help textual understanding, provide reliable historical context, and supply valuable criticism and illustration. Use such works as aids but verify their claims.
